response:
The basic chemical building block of matter, which is the simplest chemical substance, is called an "element." 

Elements are fundamental substances that cannot be broken down into simpler substances through ordinary physical or chemical means. They consist solely of one type of atom with specific numbers of protons in their nuclei (atomic number). Examples of elements include hydrogen, carbon, oxygen, nitrogen, iron, gold, etc., each having unique properties determined by the number of protons they possess.

In contrast, compounds are formed when two or more different elements chemically combine in fixed proportions. Compounds contain atoms from multiple types of elements bonded together via covalent or ionic bonds. Examples of common compounds include water (H₂O), table salt (NaCl), sulfuric acid (H₂SO₄), and glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆).

Thus, elements represent the foundational units of all matter in nature, consisting only of one kind of atom, making them essential components at the atomic level.
